newsitem.title: LATVIA: PM SHKELE OPTIMISTIC ON BALANCED BUDGETS.
newsitem.headline: PM SHKELE OPTIMISTIC ON BALANCED BUDGETS.

text.p: Latvia's Prime Minister Andris Shkele said on Thursday that he believed Latvia would achieve balanced budgets in 1997 as well as for the two year budget for 1998 and 1999.
"As for the general budget, I think it will be balanced," Shkele told Reuters in an interview.
He added that eventual problems could appear in the local authorities' budget.
Local authorities can only borrow 20 million lats from the state treasury, so the conseqences of a failure in this part is limited, he said.
"The total budget of the whole state is over one billion so this is not very much," he said.
Shkele also cautioned that the budget estimates for tax revenue could be on the high side.
"Maybe, the figures we have estimated for the near future have been too optimistic," he said.
For 1998 and 1999, the Latvian government is planning a two year budget.
"We are looking forward to a two year balanced budget. I think it will be balanced also that time," he said.
